rationale: The production roadmap requires Vault-compatible secret lifecycle controls before AEIS can be considered production-ready. This change adds a strict secret backend policy for staging/production, a value-safe add/validate/rotate lifecycle service, API endpoints for the lifecycle flow, and startup rejection for plaintext/file/memory secret backends in strict environments. It is D4 because secret storage and rotation are cross-cutting operational security controls.

steps: Remove sylion.security.secret_lifecycle and its API routes from secret_routes.py.
Restore key_store_unified.rotate to its previous signature if downstream callers require it.
Remove the SYLION_SECRETS_BACKEND startup policy from startup_check.py.
Remove lifecycle route/unit tests and this freeze document.
Run startup_check, key_store_unified and secret_routes regression tests.

fidelity_test.description: Verify that strict environments accept only SOPS/Vault-style secret backends, enforce rotation <= 90 days, and complete add/validate/rotate without returning plaintext values.
pre_conditions: Tests use in-memory stores and fixture values only.
RBAC is disabled only inside isolated route tests.
steps: Run the /secrets/create regression that previously failed on a missing vault DB directory.
fidelity_test.expected_outcome: Dummy lifecycle status is pass, strict startup policy rejects unsafe backends and long rotations, no response contains fixture secret values, and vault file stores create missing parent directories.
